title: {{NAME}} and the Fairy Who Fixed the Robot
moral: It is okay to ask for help when something is hard.
character_anchor: Bright children's book cartoon illustration, bold outlines, vivid flat colours. {{NAME}}, a young boy with brown hair and blue eyes, wearing a bright orange t-shirt with a small gear print, navy blue overalls, and chunky white trainers — same child, same face, same exact outfit in every image.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} found a big round robot in the park.
The robot sat under an old oak tree.
He was not moving at all.
Fluffy grey squirrels climbed over his arms.
His eyes were dim and dark.

pages.content:
{{NAME}} patted the robot on the arm.
"Are you okay?" he asked.
The robot gave a weak little flicker.
"My heart gear is broken," said the robot.
{{NAME}} frowned. He did not know how to fix that.

pages.content:
A tiny green fairy zoomed down from the oak tree.
She had wings like a leaf and bright gold eyes.
"I can fix things!" she said loudly.
She flew right inside the robot's chest panel.
Sparks and little lights flew out.

pages.content:
Bang! Click! Whirr!
The fairy flew back out, covered in tiny sparks.
Then the robot's eyes lit up bright blue.
He lifted both his arms up high.
"I am fixed!" he said in a warm, deep voice.

pages.content:
The robot walked slowly through the park.
He was gentle and careful around the animals.
He and the fairy bowed to each other.
{{NAME}} held the robot's big warm hand.
He felt safe and happy and very sleepy.
Goodnight, {{NAME}}. Tomorrow the fairy says the robot needs one more adventure with you.
